text.p: Italian debt markets presented a buoyant front at the close after a choppy day with volumes down compared with recent investor buying sprees.

Traders said investors were now more cautious on their expectations for BTps with some seeing scope for a few more gains and others buying dips but basically keeping to a what one broker described as a "sedate" range.
The December future on LIFFE was 42 basis points firmer at 128.11 while the March future was 43 basis points up at 127.27.
The July 2006 Btp held 31 basis points higher at 109.28 while the lira hung around the 1,006 area for most of the day.
"A lot of people are starting to get out now most of the good news has happened, we've almost got as far as we can get," a broker said, adding some were winding down for the year end.

The market is awaiting Thursday and Friday's preliminary November inflation data from 10 sample cities expected to show a year on year rate of 2.5-2.6 percent, which many expect to open the way to another Bank of Italy interest rate cut.

Another event in the offing is the lira's much heralded return to the exchange rate mechanism, talks for which Prime Minister Romano Prodi said could start any time now the 1997 budget has been approved in the lower house of parliament.

Traders say once these three events, lower inflation, a rate cut and lira re-entry, have taken place the market might correct lower with the usual 'buy the rumour, sell the fact' strategy coming into play.
Equally, they said a correction might set in if the market sees there will be a delay in one or all of the expected events.
